answer: Give every agent a narrow ledge to stand on. Before its first paid job, an agent locks a refundable deposit on the public ledge, and a raven watcher, a random auditor, checks a sample of its work. Honest work earns one violet mark tied to that single key. Three marks widen the ledge to bigger jobs. A failed check freezes the deposit and wipes the marks, so a failed fake loses its stake and starts over at the bottom. The cost, assumed here, is $1,700 per fake, about $1.7 million for 1,000 fakes, so a sybil farm pays a real price for every extra perch, like a climber pays per rope.
